title: Who's in the cabinet?
summary_cn: 英国新任首相安迪·伯纳姆开始组建内阁，任命了财政大臣约翰·希利、外交大臣埃德·米利班德等关键职位。新内阁成员包括多位前政府官员和党内重要人物，伯纳姆承诺将权力从白厅下放，加强水务和能源领域的公共控制，并建造更多市政住房。
paragraphs_en: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has started building his new cabinet after taking office following the resignation of Sir Keir Starmer.
Tap or click on a cabinet member in our interactive guide below to learn more about them and their role in government. The guide will be updated as new appointments are made.
Andy Burnham is the new prime minister, after winning the backing of 379 of Labour's 403 MPs as the best person to replace Sir Keir Starmer.

He has pledged to shift power away from Whitehall, introduce "greater public control" of the water and energy sectors and to build more council houses â while keeping Labourâs election pledge not to raise the main rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance.
Born in Aintree in 1970, Burnham was inspired by the minersâ strike to join the Labour Party in his teens and first became an MP in 2001.

The former health secretary had twice failed to become party leader - losing to Ed Miliband in 2010 and Jeremy Corbyn in 2015 - and after leaving Parliament, served as Greater Manchester mayor. He returned as Makerfield MP in June and succeeded Sir Keir Starmer a month later.

A life-long Everton fan and talented sportsman, he was part of Labour's Demon Eyes FC football team when Tony Blair was PM, and regularly featured in the Labour MPs vs Lobby journalists match while in Parliament.
John Healey has returned to the cabinet as chancellor of the exchequer, less than two months after quitting as defence secretary.

In his resignation letter Healey was highly critical of the government's defence spending plans, saying Sir Keir Starmer had been "unable" and the Treasury was "unwilling to commit the resources the nation needs to defend the country".
It is a surprise appointment for the MP for Rawmarsh and Conisbrough in South Yorkshire, with many speculating the role would go to Ed Miliband or Shabana Mahmood.
Healey was parliamentary private secretary to Chancellor Gordon Brown from 1999 to 2001, before serving as adult skills, Treasury, local government and housing minister between 2001 and 2010.
He is well-respected on the international stage and has built links with key economic allies in Europe, the Middle East and the United States.
Louise Haigh has become chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, first secretary of state and Cabinet Office minister.
Haigh, one of Andy Burnhamâs closest allies, will run the Cabinet Office, the department that supports the prime minister and co-ordinates the governmentâs policies to deliver its agenda.

After entering parliament as MP for Sheffield Heeley in 2015, Haigh was named the hardest-working new MP in 2016 due to the number of her Commons speeches and questions, and praised by then-Speaker John Bercow for her "terrier-like intensity".

In 2025, the former special constable and Unite union shop steward became the first person to resign from Sir Keir Starmerâs cabinet as transport secretary after it emerged that she had admitted a fraud offence in 2013.
On the backbenches she emerged as a crucial power broker on Labour's "soft left", and was at the heart of the huge rebellion that scuppered the government's welfare cuts in 2025.
Ed Miliband is the new foreign secretary, moving from the energy and net zero brief he has held since Labour returned to power.
He had been touted as a possible chancellor, but opinion was divided between supporters who pointed to his experience in the Treasury, and opponents who distrusted his views, particularly on energy.

Since the election he has spoken out against those urging the government to drop its net zero ambitions and insisted the party's green power transition will help secure social justice and national security.

Miliband has been the MP for Doncaster North since 2005 but has been at the centre of Labour politics for even longer - working for Labour MPs before the 1997 election win and as a special adviser to Gordon Brown when he became chancellor.

He is best known as a former Labour leader - having beaten his brother David, among others, in the leadership contest that followed the partyâs 2010 general election defeat - but has also co-hosted the Reasons to be Cheerful podcast since 2017.
Shabana Mahmood remains home secretary, the position she has held since September 2025.
Mahmood, who has a reputation among Labour MPs as a hardliner on immigration, is responsible for that brief in the role, along with national security and for policing in England and Wales.
Shortly after being appointed, she announced sweeping changes to the UKâs asylum system, brushing off criticism from some Labour MPs and describing the previous system as âout of controlâ.

A former national campaign co-ordinator for Labour, Mahmood oversaw the party's Batley & Spen by-election win in 2021 which some have credited with saving Sir Keir Starmerâs leadership following a defeat in Hartlepool months earlier.

The Birmingham Ladywood MP claims to be the first female Muslim MP - although she was elected in 2010 alongside Yasmin Qureshi and Rushanara Ali - because, she says, her count was the first completed on the night.
Wes Streeting is the new defence secretary, replacing Dan Jarvis who had only been in the role for a matter of weeks.

Streeting, who resigned as health secretary in May saying he had lost confidence in Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister, eventually decided to back Andy Burnham rather than launch his own leadership bid.
The former National Union of Students president and London councillor is widely seen as one of the partyâs most skilled communicators.

He has written an autobiography about growing up in a council flat in Londonâs East End, visiting his bank robber grandfather in jail, growing up as a gay Christian and about being diagnosed and treated for kidney cancer at the age of 38.

The Ilford North MP has said his upbringing left him "quite cynical" of the role of the state compared with many Labour colleagues, aware of its failings as well as its potential to enable opportunity.

Yvette Cooper remains in cabinet but in a new role as health and social care secretary, having most recently served as foreign secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government and home secretary before that.

She was first elected as an MP for Yorkshire seat of Pontefract and Castleford in 1997 and went to serve as the first female chief secretary to the Treasury, later becoming work and pensions secretary in the Labour government.
After the 2010 election defeat for Labour, she took on the role of shadow home secretary. She now represents Pontefract, Castleford and Knottingley.

Among other firsts in her political career, the former journalist became the first minister to take maternity leave, and she was one half of the first married couple in the cabinet - alongside her husband, former education secretary and Strictly Come Dancing contestant, Ed Balls.
Lucy Powell has been appointed as education secretary.

Powell had been leader of the House of Commons - responsible for delivering the government's legislative programme - until she was sacked by Sir Keir Starmer in the reshuffle that followed Angela Rayner's resignation from the cabinet.
She went on to replace Rayner as deputy leader of the party, winning an election of Labour members.

Powell, who joined the Labour Party at 15, has been an MP since winning a by-election in Manchester Central in 2012 and has held several shadow cabinet roles, including stints leading on education, housing and culture.

She led Ed Miliband's successful campaign to become Labour leader in 2010, helping him defeat Andy Burnham among others, and was then Miliband's chief of staff for two years. However, as a Manchester MP she has also worked closely with Burnham for many years.
Pat McFadden remains work and pensions secretary, the role he has held since September 2025.
He took over the department months after the party was forced to U-turn on extensive changes designed to reduce the welfare bill.

As the partyâs national campaign co-ordinator McFadden was one of the masterminds behind Labourâs historic 2024 election victory, constantly stressing the need for message discipline ahead of the election and warning activists and MPs alike to ignore the opinion polls.

A former adviser to Sir Tony Blair, the Glasgow-born MP has represented the Wolverhampton South East constituency since 2005, serving as a business minister under Gordon Brown and in several shadow ministerial roles since then.

McFadden has also held the post of chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, responsible for running the Cabinet Office - the department that supports the prime minister and co-ordinates the governmentâs policies to deliver its agenda.
Angela Rayner has returned to the cabinet as secretary of state for housing, communities and local government, months after settling her tax affairs with HM Revenue and Customs.

She quit as Sir Keir Starmerâs deputy PM and housing secretary after the then prime ministerâs independent ethics adviser found that she had broken the ministerial code by underpaying stamp duty when she bought a flat in May 2025.

Born in Stockport, Greater Manchester, in 1980, Rayner grew up on one of the area's poorest council estates and from an early age, was caring for her mother, who had bipolar disorder and suffered from depression.
She left school with no qualifications but, after having her first child at 16, Rayner studied part-time at college, gained a vocational qualification in social care.

As she worked as a care worker in Stockport, she also rose quickly through the ranks of the union Unison, and she credits the union movement for encouraging her to enter politics. She became MP for Ashton-under-Lyne in 2015 and is a powerful figure on Labour's "soft left".
Jonathan Reynolds has become secretary of state for business, innovation, science and trade.
It is a return to the business department he led until September 2025 but the role has been expanded to take in science and innovation, which were in a separate department.

The son of a fireman, Reynolds grew up in Sunderland - and still supports the cityâs football club - but he went to university in Manchester, where he joined the Labour Party and chose to remain after graduating.

Reynolds, who has described himself as a Christian socialist, has been the MP for Stalybridge and Hyde in Greater Manchester since 2010 - he had been an assistant to the constituencyâs previous MP James Purnell.
Bridget Phillipson will remain in cabinet as women and equalities minister but will no longer be education secretary.
Before becoming an MP she managed a refuge for women and children who were fleeing domestic violence.

Raised by her mother in a small terrace council house with rotting window frames and no upstairs heating in a former mining town near Sunderland, she was bullied at school and received free school meals.
But Phillipson credits "amazing teachers" for encouraging her to apply to Oxford, where she studied modern history.
She had joined Labour aged 15 and became its MP for Houghton and Sunderland South in 2010, aged 26. She has been a member of Sir Keir Starmerâs top team since he became Labour leader.
Former Labour leadership challenger Lisa Nandy remains digital, culture, media and sport secretary.

In the role she has held negotiations with the BBC about how it will be funded in the future and has said she is thinking "quite radically and creatively" about alternatives to the "deeply regressive" licence fee.
Nandy stood against Sir Keir Starmer in the 2020 leadership race and was described as ârefreshingly untribalâ by one Tory MP who thought she was Labourâs best choice.

She finished third but her reward was to become shadow foreign secretary. 
                        Nandy later shadowed Levelling Up Secretary Michael Gove before moving to international development.

As co-founder of the Centre for Towns think tank, Nandy has been a vocal champion of places like Wigan, which she has represented since 2010, arguing they have been overlooked in discussions on regional development and devolution.
Miatta Fahnbulleh has been named energy security and net zero secretary, replacing Ed Miliband who has become foreign secretary.
She had been working on policy ideas for a potential Burnham government since resigning as a junior communities minister in the aftermath of Labour's disastrous local election results in May.
Born in Liberia, she was brought to the UK as a five-year-old by her parents who were fleeing the countryâs civil war in 1986 - the family were granted asylum in the late 1980s.
A trained economist, she is a former civil servant and also ran the New Economics Foundation think tank before becoming MP for Peckham in London in 2024.
She is seen as being part of Labourâs "soft left" faction.
Former Home Office minister Alex Norris has been promoted to the role of justice secretary and Lord Chancellor.
The former Trade Union organiser and Nottingham City councillor was first elected to Parliament in 2017.
In the Home Office he was responsible for border security and asylum.
The Nottingham North and Kimberley MP, who was born in Manchester, describes himself as a keen runner and Manchester City supporter.
Dame Angela Eagle has been promoted to the cabinet as secretary of state for environment, food and rural affairs.
She was previously a minister in the Home Office and Cabinet Office and has been on the Labour front bench since the last Labour government.
Eagle is perhaps best known for challenging the leadership of Jeremy Corbyn in 2016 - but withdrawing to back rival Owen Smith days later.
She has been MP for Wallasey since 1992 and was joined in the Commons in 1997 by her identical twin sister Maria Eagle.
Sir Chris Bryant has been appointed secretary of state for Northern Ireland, replacing Hilary Benn.
He moves from the Department for Business and Trade.
Itâs Sir Chrisâs first cabinet position, although he held a number of shadow frontbench roles under Sir Kier Starmer and Jeremy Corbyn.
Sir Chris, a former Anglican priest, was awarded a knighthood in 2023 in recognition of his campaigning work around acquired brain injury and melanoma - a type of skin cancer.
He was elected as the MP for Rhondda and Ogmore (previously Rhondda) on 7 June 2001.
Douglas Alexander stays in the cabinet as Scotland secretary, having previously been in the cabinets of Keir Starmer, Gordon Brown and Tony Blair.

A former secretary of state for international development and for transport, Alexander lost his Paisley and Renfrewshire South seat to the SNP in one of the biggest shocks of the 2015 general election.

He was re-elected to parliament in 2024 as MP for Lothian East and was tipped for an immediate return to cabinet, but Sir Keir Starmer initially appointed him as a trade and economic security minister.
Alexander told the BBC he hadnât missed âthe game of politicsâ or the âbrutality of social mediaâ but had been asked to stand for re-election by local party members.
Stephen Kinnock has been named secretary of state for Wales.
He had been the care minister since Labour won the general election in 2024.
The son of former Labour leader Neil Kinnock, he joined the Labour Party aged 15 during the miners' strike and has been MP since 2015.
He is married to the former prime minister of Denmark Helle Thorning-Schmidt.
Anneliese Midgley, one of the key figures in Andy Burnham's leadership campaign, has been promoted to the cabinet in the role of chief whip.

She has only been the MP for Knowsley, not far from Makerfield, since 2024 but she has been an influential force in the Labour movement for much longer than that, working for both Sir Keir Starmer and Jeremy Corbyn in opposition, following stints at the TUC.
She has spoken about how, when she was growing up, her familyâs life was changed by the "secure, well-paid, unionised job" her father got at a car factory.
Before her political career, music lover Midgey ran club nights in Liverpool, worked in record shops and helped bands including Pulp with press.

She was briefly married to Bob Stanley, a member of indie group Saint Etienne, and has told how the couple shared their first kiss on hearing that Tory grandee and TV personality Michael Portillo had lost his seat in the 1997 election.

paragraphs_cn: 首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在基尔·斯塔默爵士（Sir Keir Starmer）辞职后上任，已开始组建新内阁。
点击或轻触下方互动指南中的内阁成员，了解他们及其在政府中的角色。该指南将随着新任命而更新。
安迪·伯纳姆成为新任首相，他在工党403名议员中获得379人支持，被视为接替基尔·斯塔默爵士的最佳人选。
他承诺将权力从白厅下放，对水和能源部门实施“更大的公共控制”，并建造更多市政住房——同时保留工党不提高所得税、增值税或国民保险主要税率的竞选承诺。
伯纳姆1970年出生于安特里（Aintree），受矿工罢工启发，十几岁时加入工党，2001年首次成为议员。
这位前卫生大臣曾两次竞选党魁失败——2010年输给埃德·米利班德（Ed Miliband），2015年输给杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn）——离开议会后，担任大曼彻斯特市长。他于6月重返议会，成为梅克菲尔德（Makerfield）选区议员，一个月后接替基尔·斯塔默爵士。
作为终身埃弗顿球迷和才华横溢的运动员，他在托尼·布莱尔（Tony Blair）任首相时曾是工党“恶魔之眼FC”足球队成员，并在议会期间经常参加工党议员对游说记者的比赛。
约翰·希利（John Healey）重返内阁担任财政大臣，距离他辞去国防大臣不到两个月。
在辞职信中，希利严厉批评政府的国防开支计划，称基尔·斯塔默爵士“无法”而财政部“不愿承诺国家保卫所需资源”。
这对南约克郡罗默什和科尼斯布鲁（Rawmarsh and Conisbrough）选区议员来说是一个意外任命，许多人猜测该职位将由埃德·米利班德或沙巴纳·马哈茂德（Shabana Mahmood）担任。
希利在1999年至2001年间担任财政大臣戈登·布朗（Gordon Brown）的议会私人秘书，随后在2001年至2010年间担任成人技能、财政、地方政府和住房部长。
他在国际舞台上备受尊敬，并与欧洲、中东和美国的关键经济盟友建立了联系。
路易丝·海格（Louise Haigh）成为兰开斯特公爵领地大臣、首席国务大臣和内阁办公室大臣。
海格是安迪·伯纳姆最亲密的盟友之一，将负责内阁办公室，该部门支持首相并协调政府政策以落实议程。
2015年作为谢菲尔德希利（Sheffield Heeley）选区议员进入议会后，海格因在下议院的演讲和提问数量而被评为2016年最勤奋的新议员，并因“梗犬般的强度”受到时任议长约翰·伯考（John Bercow）的赞扬。
2025年，这位前特别警员和联合工会（Unite）车间代表成为首位从基尔·斯塔默爵士内阁辞职的人，此前她承认在2013年犯有欺诈罪。
在后座议员中，她成为工党“温和左派”的关键权力掮客，并处于2025年破坏政府福利削减的大规模叛乱的核心。
埃德·米利班德（Ed Miliband）成为新任外交大臣，从工党重新执政以来一直负责的能源和净零事务调任。
他曾被吹捧为可能的财政大臣，但支持者指出他在财政部的经验，而反对者则不相信他的观点，尤其是在能源方面。
自大选以来，他公开反对那些敦促政府放弃净零目标的人，并坚称该党的绿色能源转型将有助于确保社会正义和国家安全。
米利班德自2005年起担任唐卡斯特北（Doncaster North）选区议员，但他在工党政治中心的时间更长——在1997年大选胜利前为工党议员工作，并在戈登·布朗成为财政大臣时担任其特别顾问。
他最出名的是前工党领袖——在2010年大选失败后的党魁竞选中击败了包括他兄弟大卫在内的对手——但自2017年以来，他还共同主持了播客《快乐的理由》（Reasons to be Cheerful）。
沙巴纳·马哈茂德（Shabana Mahmood）留任内政大臣，她自2025年9月起担任该职位。
马哈茂德在工党议员中以移民问题强硬派著称，负责该领域的移民事务，以及英格兰和威尔士的国家安全和警务。
被任命后不久，她宣布对英国庇护制度进行彻底改革，无视一些工党议员的批评，并将之前的制度描述为“失控”。
作为工党前全国竞选协调员，马哈茂德监督了该党2021年巴特利和斯彭（Batley & Spen）补选的胜利，一些人认为这拯救了基尔·斯塔默爵士的领导地位，此前几个月在哈特尔普尔（Hartlepool）遭遇失败。
这位伯明翰莱迪伍德（Birmingham Ladywood）选区议员自称是第一位女性穆斯林议员——尽管她与亚斯敏·库雷希（Yasmin Qureshi）和鲁沙纳拉·阿里（Rushanara Ali）于2010年同时当选——因为她表示自己的计票是当晚最先完成的。
韦斯·斯特里廷（Wes Streeting）成为新任国防大臣，接替仅任职数周的丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）。
斯特里廷于5月辞去卫生大臣职务，称对基尔·斯塔默爵士作为首相失去信心，最终决定支持安迪·伯纳姆，而非自己发起领导权竞选。
这位前全国学生联合会主席和伦敦议员被广泛视为党内最善于沟通的人之一。
他写了一本自传，讲述在伦敦东区市政公寓长大、探望因抢劫银行入狱的祖父、作为同性恋基督徒成长以及38岁时被诊断并治疗肾癌的经历。
这位伊尔福德北（Ilford North）选区议员表示，与许多工党同事相比，他的成长经历让他对国家的角色“相当怀疑”，既意识到其失败之处，也看到其创造机会的潜力。
伊薇特·库珀（Yvette Cooper）留任内阁，但担任卫生和社会关怀大臣新职务，此前她在基尔·斯塔默爵士政府中担任外交大臣，再之前是内政大臣。
她于1997年首次当选为约克郡庞特弗拉克特和卡斯尔福德（Pontefract and Castleford）选区议员，并担任首位女性财政部首席秘书，后来在工党政府中成为工作和养老金大臣。
在2010年工党大选失败后，她担任影子内政大臣。她现在代表庞特弗拉克特、卡斯尔福德和诺丁利（Pontefract, Castleford and Knottingley）。
在她的政治生涯中，这位前记者成为首位休产假的大臣，并且是内阁中第一对已婚夫妇的一半——她的丈夫是前教育大臣和《舞动奇迹》参赛者埃德·鲍尔斯（Ed Balls）。
露西·鲍威尔（Lucy Powell）被任命为教育大臣。
鲍威尔曾担任下议院领袖——负责交付政府的立法计划——直到安吉拉·雷纳（Angela Rayner）辞去内阁职务后的改组中被基尔·斯塔默爵士解雇。
她随后接替雷纳成为工党副领袖，在工党成员选举中获胜。
鲍威尔15岁加入工党，自2012年在曼彻斯特中央（Manchester Central）补选中获胜以来一直担任议员，并担任过多个影子内阁职务，包括负责教育、住房和文化。
她在2010年领导了埃德·米利班德成功竞选工党领袖的活动，帮助他击败了安迪·伯纳姆等人，随后担任米利班德的幕僚长两年。然而，作为曼彻斯特议员，她也与伯纳姆密切合作多年。
帕特·麦克法登（Pat McFadden）留任工作和养老金大臣，他自2025年9月起担任该职务。
他在该党被迫在旨在减少福利账单的广泛改革上180度大转弯几个月后接管了该部门。
作为工党全国竞选协调员，麦克法登是工党2024年历史性大选胜利的策划者之一，不断强调选前信息纪律的必要性，并警告活动家和议员忽视民调。
这位出生于格拉斯哥的议员曾是托尼·布莱尔爵士的顾问，自2005年以来代表伍尔弗汉普顿东南（Wolverhampton South East）选区，在戈登·布朗手下担任商业部长，此后担任多个影子部长职务。
麦克法登还担任过兰开斯特公爵领地大臣，负责管理内阁办公室——该部门支持首相并协调政府政策以落实议程。
安吉拉·雷纳（Angela Rayner）重返内阁，担任住房、社区和地方政府大臣，几个月前她与英国税务海关总署（HM Revenue and Customs）解决了税务问题。
在时任首相的独立道德顾问发现她于2025年5月购买公寓时少付印花税、违反大臣守则后，她辞去了基尔·斯塔默爵士的副首相和住房大臣职务。
雷纳1980年出生于大曼彻斯特斯托克波特（Stockport），在该地区最贫困的市政住宅区长大，从小照顾患有双相情感障碍和抑郁症的母亲。
她离开学校时没有学历，但在16岁生下第一个孩子后，她在学院兼职学习，获得了社会护理职业资格。
在斯托克波特担任护理员期间，她在联合工会（Unison）中迅速晋升，并归功于工会运动鼓励她进入政界。她于2015年成为阿什顿安德莱恩（Ashton-under-Lyne）选区议员，是工党“温和左派”的有力人物。
乔纳森·雷诺兹（Jonathan Reynolds）成为商业、创新、科学和贸易大臣。
这是他重返领导至2025年9月的商业部门，但该角色已扩大，包括科学和创新，这些此前属于独立部门。
作为消防员的儿子，雷诺兹在桑德兰（Sunderland）长大——仍然支持该市的足球俱乐部——但在曼彻斯特上大学，在那里加入工党，并选择毕业后留下。
雷诺兹自称是基督教社会主义者，自2010年以来担任大曼彻斯特斯特利布里奇和海德（Stalybridge and Hyde）选区议员——他曾是该选区前任议员詹姆斯·珀内尔（James Purnell）的助理。
布里奇特·菲利普森（Bridget Phillipson）将留任内阁，担任妇女和平等部长，但不再担任教育大臣。
在成为议员之前，她管理着一个为逃离家庭暴力的妇女和儿童设立的庇护所。
她在桑德兰附近一个前矿业小镇由母亲抚养长大，住在窗框腐烂、楼上没有暖气的排屋市政住宅中，在学校被欺负，并享受免费校餐。
但菲利普森感谢“了不起的老师”鼓励她申请牛津大学，在那里学习现代史。
她15岁加入工党，2010年26岁时成为霍顿和桑德兰南（Houghton and Sunderland South）选区议员。自基尔·斯塔默爵士成为工党领袖以来，她一直是其高级团队的一员。
前工党领袖挑战者丽莎·南迪（Lisa Nandy）留任数字、文化、媒体和体育大臣。
在该职位上，她与BBC就未来资金方式进行了谈判，并表示正在“相当激进和创造性地”思考“严重累退的”电视许可费的替代方案。
南迪在2020年领导权竞选中与基尔·斯塔默爵士竞争，被一位认为她是工党最佳选择的保守党议员描述为“令人耳目一新的非部落化”。
她获得第三名，但奖励是成为影子外交大臣。南迪后来负责影子升级大臣迈克尔·戈夫（Michael Gove），然后转向国际发展。
作为智库“城镇中心”（Centre for Towns）的联合创始人，南迪一直是像维冈（Wigan）这样的地方的有力倡导者，她自2010年以来代表该选区，认为这些地方在区域发展和权力下放的讨论中被忽视。
米亚塔·法恩布勒（Miatta Fahnbulleh）被任命为能源安全和净零大臣，接替成为外交大臣的埃德·米利班德。
自5月工党地方选举结果灾难性后辞去社区初级部长职务以来，她一直在为潜在的伯纳姆政府制定政策思路。
她出生于利比里亚，1986年5岁时被逃离内战的父母带到英国——该家庭在1980年代末获得庇护。
作为训练有素的经济学家，她曾是公务员，并在2024年成为伦敦佩卡姆（Peckham）选区议员之前运营新经济基金会（New Economics Foundation）智库。
她被视为工党“温和左派”派系的一员。
前内政部大臣亚历克斯·诺里斯（Alex Norris）被提升为司法大臣和大法官。
这位前工会组织者和诺丁汉市议员于2017年首次当选议员。
在内政部，他负责边境安全和庇护。
这位诺丁汉北和金伯利（Nottingham North and Kimberley）选区议员出生于曼彻斯特，自称是热衷跑步者和曼城支持者。
安吉拉·伊格尔女爵士（Dame Angela Eagle）被提升为内阁环境、食品和农村事务大臣。
她此前是内政部和内阁办公室的部长，自上一届工党政府以来一直担任工党前座议员。
伊格尔最出名的是在2016年挑战杰里米·科尔宾的领导权——但几天后退出支持对手欧文·史密斯（Owen Smith）。
她自1992年起担任沃拉西（Wallasey）选区议员，1997年她的同卵双胞胎妹妹玛丽亚·伊格尔（Maria Eagle）也进入下议院。
克里斯·布莱恩特爵士（Sir Chris Bryant）被任命为北爱尔兰事务大臣，接替希拉里·本（Hilary Benn）。
他从商业和贸易部调任。
这是克里斯爵士的第一个内阁职位，尽管他在基尔·斯塔默爵士和杰里米·科尔宾领导下担任过多个影子前座职务。
克里斯爵士曾是英国圣公会牧师，2023年因在获得性脑损伤和黑色素瘤（一种皮肤癌）方面的倡导工作被授予爵士头衔。
他于2001年6月7日当选为朗达和奥格莫尔（Rhondda and Ogmore）（前身为朗达）选区议员。
道格拉斯·亚历山大（Douglas Alexander）留任内阁担任苏格兰事务大臣，此前曾在基尔·斯塔默、戈登·布朗和托尼·布莱尔的内阁任职。
作为前国际发展和交通大臣，亚历山大在2015年大选的最大意外之一中，将佩斯利和伦弗鲁郡南（Paisley and Renfrewshire South）席位输给了苏格兰民族党。
他于2024年作为洛锡安东（Lothian East）选区议员重新当选议员，并被看好立即重返内阁，但基尔·斯塔默爵士最初任命他为贸易和经济安全部长。
亚历山大告诉BBC，他并不怀念“政治游戏”或“社交媒体的残酷”，但应地方党部成员的要求再次参选。
斯蒂芬·金诺克（Stephen Kinnock）被任命为威尔士事务大臣。
自工党在2024年大选中获胜以来，他一直担任护理部长。
作为前工党领袖尼尔·金诺克（Neil Kinnock）的儿子，他在15岁矿工罢工期间加入工党，自2015年起担任议员。
他与丹麦前首相赫勒·托宁-施密特（Helle Thorning-Schmidt）结婚。
安内莉斯·米奇利（Anneliese Midgley）是安迪·伯纳姆领导权竞选的关键人物之一，被提升为内阁担任首席党鞭。
她自2024年起才担任距离梅克菲尔德不远的诺斯利（Knowsley）选区议员，但她在工党运动中的影响力远不止于此，曾在反对党时期为基尔·斯塔默爵士和杰里米·科尔宾工作，此前在工会大会（TUC）任职。
她曾谈到，在她成长过程中，父亲在汽车工厂获得的“稳定、高薪、工会化的工作”改变了家庭生活。
在从政之前，音乐爱好者米奇利在利物浦经营夜店，在唱片店工作，并帮助包括果浆（Pulp）在内的乐队处理媒体事务。
她曾与独立乐队圣艾蒂安（Saint Etienne）成员鲍勃·斯坦利（Bob Stanley）短暂结婚，并讲述了两人在听到保守党大佬兼电视名人迈克尔·波蒂略（Michael Portillo）在1997年大选中失去席位时初吻的故事。

keywords.definition_en: to make a formal promise to do something

keywords.definition_en: the act of giving up a job or position

keywords.definition_en: to guess about something without having enough information
keywords.context_sentence: It is a surprise appointment for the MP for Rawmarsh and Conisbrough in South Yorkshire, with many speculating the role would go to Ed Miliband or Shabana Mahmood.

keywords.definition_en: to organize the different parts of an activity so that they work together
keywords.context_sentence: Haigh will run the Cabinet Office, the department that supports the prime minister and co-ordinates the government’s policies to deliver its agenda.

keywords.definition_en: an organized attempt to change a government or authority
keywords.context_sentence: On the backbenches she emerged as a crucial power broker on Labour's 'soft left', and was at the heart of the huge rebellion that scuppered the government's welfare cuts in 2025.
keywords.context_translation: 在后座议员中，她成为工党“温和左派”的关键权力掮客，并是2025年挫败政府福利削减计划的大规模反抗的核心人物。

keywords.definition_en: to try to persuade people that someone or something is important or good

keywords.definition_en: a person who supports extreme or uncompromising policies
keywords.context_sentence: Mahmood, who has a reputation among Labour MPs as a hardliner on immigration, is responsible for that brief in the role, along with national security and for policing in England and Wales.
